taxpayer.notes: Former C.P.A.; pleaded guilty to bank fraud; took full ESOP/401(k) distribution in Feb. 2016 at age 43 to pay restitution; incarcerated July 2016 - July 2017. Filing status not stated.

notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Inclusion of distribution (never received/benefited), 72(t) tax (relied on withholding), late-filing addition
conceded: Respondent conceded the sec. 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty

findings_of_fact.fact: Elected full distribution from Principal retirement account in Feb. 2016; estimated value $108,802.88
findings_of_fact.snippet: The estimated value of the account at the time of the election was $108,802.88.

findings_of_fact.fact: Check for $82,924.72 issued after withholding federal tax $21,894 and state tax ~$4,652; endorsed to PCG and credited to restitution
findings_of_fact.snippet: Principal issued petitioner a check for $82,924.72 after withholding Federal income tax of $21,894 and State income tax of approximately $4,652.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner was 43 at the time of the distribution
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner was 43 years old at the time of the distribution.

findings_of_fact.fact: Principal reported taxable retirement income of $109,471
findings_of_fact.snippet: Principal reported that it had paid petitioner taxable retirement income of $109,471 during the year at issue.

findings_of_fact.fact: Respondent determined sec. 72(t) additional tax of $10,947
findings_of_fact.snippet: Respondent also determined an additional tax of $10,947 under section 72(t)

findings_of_fact.fact: No exception (e.g., rollover) argued or established; qualified trust undisputed
findings_of_fact.snippet: He has neither argued nor established that an exception applies.

findings_of_fact.fact: Distribution not used for any expense qualifying for a 72(t) exception
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner did not use the distribution for the payment of any expense that would allow him to avoid the 10% additional tax.

findings_of_fact.fact: Incarcerated July 2016 - July 2017; tried but unable to file return or extension by due date
findings_of_fact.snippet: he was unable to access the resources he needed to file his return or a request for extension by the due date.
He filed the return on September 4, 2017.
We found his testimony credible, especially in the light of his postrelease conduct.

issues.question: Is the $109,471 distribution from petitioner's ESOP/401(k) retirement account includible in his 2016 gross income?
issues.holding: Yes; distribution was paid to him and applied to his restitution; no exception
issues.computable_reason: Distribution from qualified 401(a) trust actually distributed and not rolled over is includible under sec. 402(a)

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the 10% additional tax under sec. 72(t) on the distribution?
issues.holding: Liable; petitioner was 43 (under 59-1/2) and no exception applies; entire distribution subject to 10% tax

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the sec. 6651(a)(1) addition to tax for 2016?
issues.holding: Not liable; reasonable cause shown (incarceration plus credible diligent attempts to file)
issues.computable_reason: Reasonable cause finding based on credibility of testimony

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent as to the deficiency and for petitioner as to the accuracy-related penalty under section 6662(a) and the addition to tax under section 6651(a)(1).
decision.summary: Deficiency sustained ($109,471 includible; 10% 72(t) tax); no 6662(a) penalty (conceded); no 6651(a)(1) addition (reasonable cause)

notes: Some facts stipulated. Tenth Circuit (Erickson) foundation rule applied. Derived: 10% x $109,471 = $10,947.10, matching respondent's $10,947. Reliance on payer withholding no defense to 72(t) (fn. 9). Also: July 11, 2016 court ordered $135,560.12 transferred from joint account; $52,679.61 applied to restitution, $82,880.51 returned to ex-wife.
